events.text: my order was 35 minutes late tonight, order #8501 from Taqueria Luz. It was supposed to come at 7 and didn't show up until 7:35. I'd like to get something back for that.
I'm sorry about the late order. Before I look into it, I need to verify your identity. Please give me your full name and either the email address or the phone number on your account.
Sure. My full name is Marcus Lee, and the email on my account is marcus.lee@mailbox.example.

Thank you, Marcus. You're verified, and I've reviewed order K-8501.

I can't offer compensation for this one. At 6:10 PM the restaurant was running behind, so your promised time was updated to 7:25 PM. We sent that update by push notification and SMS, more than 30 minutes before the original 7:00 PM time. Under our policy the updated time is the one we measure against.

The delivery log shows the handoff at 7:35 PM. That's 10 minutes after the updated time. Credit applies only when an order arrives more than 15 minutes after the promised time, so this order doesn't qualify.

I'm sorry it was later than you expected. If there's something else wrong with the order, such as a missing or incorrect item, tell me and I'll check it.

Hmm, I did get a text around 6:10 saying the restaurant was running behind, with a new time of 7:25. But I didn't expect it to be 35 minutes late either way, and I'm not sure why the update matters if it still came later than that. My food wasn't missing or wrong, so that's not the issue.

Can you tell me more about how the new time was worked out? It still feels like I'm being charged for a delay that got longer than what I was told.

I understand why that's frustrating. Here is how it works.

**Why the update matters.** We measure lateness against the most recent time we told you, as long as we told you at least 30 minutes before the original promised time. You got the 7:25 PM update at 6:10 PM, which was 50 minutes before the original 7:00 PM. That made 7:25 PM your promised time for this order.

**How it was worked out.** I don't have the details of how the restaurant's delay produced the 7:25 PM estimate. The log only says the restaurant was running behind. The handoff was recorded at 7:35 PM, which is 10 minutes after 7:25 PM. Compensation starts at more than 15 minutes past the promised time, so this order falls short.

**Charges.** You weren't charged anything extra for the delay. The total was $35.55, made up of $27.50 in food, a $2.99 delivery fee, a $2.06 service fee and a $3.00 tip.

I can't offer a credit or refund for this delay, because our policy doesn't allow compensation outside the late-delivery rules. If you'd like to talk to a person about it, I can pass your case to a specialist who will follow up within 24 hours. I can't promise what they'll decide.

Okay, so the 7:25 was the official time once I got that text, and 7:35 is only 10 minutes past it. That's not what I expected, but I get it.

I'd like a specialist to look at it, since I think 35 minutes is a long wait even with the update. Please pass it along, and I'll wait for their follow-up.

args.summary: Customer Marcus Lee (verified account holder) asked for late-delivery compensation on K-8501 (Taqueria Luz). Original promise 7:00 PM; eta_updated to 7:25 PM sent at 6:10 PM (notified, customer confirms receiving it); handoff 7:35 PM = 10 min late vs. updated ETA, so no compensation under policy. Customer accepts the policy explanation but feels a 35-minute wait vs. the original time is too long and asked for a specialist to review. No food issues. Nothing issued.

Thanks for your patience, Marcus. Is there anything else I can help with today?
